after: ## What each "power" asks of a writer
alt: Three columns for the Power of Persuasion, Storytelling and Information, each with what the writing must do and the language choices that typically matter, from modality and calls to action, to narrative voice and pace, to signposting and layout. A note stresses defining audience and purpose precisely.
caption: Each area sets a different job, and audience and purpose decide the choices.

alt: A checklist for a style model: a published text in the same form and area as the planned piece, short enough to analyse closely, rich enough to teach techniques, and the best match for audience and purpose. Beside it: borrow technique, not content or phrasing.
caption: Pick a style model to learn technique from, not material to borrow.

after: ## Annotating the style model at the language levels
alt: Annotation that names a feature and what it does is contrasted with highlighting that only labels. Six language levels follow, each with the question to ask of the style model, from how graphology guides the reader to how discourse structure and cohesion work.
caption: Ask each level's question of the style model, and note what each feature does.

alt: Three style-model features become decisions for a speech: a present-tense one-line anecdote becomes a 2-sentence anecdote about a grandfather, triadic structures are saved for the three main turns, and a shift from "I" to "we" moves to collective address before the call to action. A final step says to adapt features to a different audience and purpose.
caption: Turn each annotation into a decision, then adapt it to your own audience and purpose.

alt: Three redrafting notes from the lesson, each pairing a change with a linguistic reason: cutting adjectives from the opening noun phrase to quicken pace, moving a statistic to the opening to establish credibility, and changing passive to active to make the council responsible.
caption: Note each change and its linguistic reason; the notes feed the commentary.

alt: Five numbered stages of the commentary: context, the style model, your choices, the writing process, and evaluation. A vertical thread beside them shows connections between the style model and the piece running throughout, and a note warns against narrating the process.
caption: Five stages, with the style model and your piece connected all the way through.

after: ## How the two parts are assessed
alt: The original writing, 750 words and 25 marks, is assessed on AO5: handling the form, controlling register, positioning the audience and writing accurately and cohesively. The commentary, also 750 words and 25 marks, draws on all the assessment objectives, including AO4 connections between the writing and the style model.
caption: The writing is judged on AO5; the commentary needs AO4 connections to the style model.
